Thanks for the recap, Markus — that matches my notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PO threshold: AP typically asks for a PO for anything > $25k per fiscal year for a single vendor. The $50k number I gave was a rough figure I remembered; sorry for the confusion.
- For a 3-month pilot at projected usage, we should be under the PO threshold and could use the corporate card route — but Procurement will still require vendor registration for risk monitoring.
- Marketplace: we love the idea of Ariba; however, listing can take 2–4 weeks (depending on your paperwork). If onboarding needs to be faster, card + vendor registration is the pragmatic path.

I'll introduce you to Tanya Brooks in AP (cc'ed on my next message) — she handles supplier setup and will confirm the exact docs needed.

Jamie

Hi Markus / team — thanks for the materials, Jamie. Quick answers from AP: 

1) Required docs: W-9, vendor registration form (we will email a portal invite), certificate of insurance (COI) for vendors doing production-facing services (pilot-level COI can be lower, we’ll confirm), and onboarding security questionnaire (brief) — SOC 2 is helpful but not always required for pilots.
2) Payment instruments: Corporate card OK for pilots where spend is expected < $25k/year and the vendor registers in our portal. For any contracted spend >= $25k we require a PO and a completed vendor risk review.
3) Marketplace: If Redwood can be added to Ariba we’ll send an invite — that generally speeds up procurement once listing is live, but initial listing may take 10–20 business days.
4) Timing: Portal invite and vendor registration link — 1 business day after you confirm contact details. Vendor onboarding + documents review — typically 3–7 business days for card-eligible pilots, 10–20 for PO path (risk review included).

Next steps from AP: Please complete the vendor onboarding checklist with Redwood's legal and banking data. I’ve placed a short checklist in the portal once you accept the invite. Once we have W-9 + bank info + COI (if applicable) we can approve for card billing.

If you want to fast-track the PO path we’ll need the MSA + SOW to start the risk review; that will likely be the slower route.

Tanya Brooks
Supplier Onboarding Lead, FlowMetrix AP
